key_insight: Orthogonalized momentum (Muon) can fail on nonsmooth convex objectives with fixed momentum, but becomes reliable when momentum is adaptive and coupled with a vanishing step size, leading to the practical MAGD method.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-parameter models in deep learning, this gives a clearer recipe for when orthogonalized momentum is safe to use and how to modify it for nonsmooth optimization.
method: Prove a failure case for Muon on locally Lipschitz convex objectives with fixed β and history-based step sizes.
Show convergence is recovered when β adapts toward 1 while the step size vanishes.
Introduce MAGD, which balances orthogonalized momentum with gradient updates based on relative progress and achieves optimal dimension-dependent rates.
evidence_signal: The paper validates the theory with experiments on synthetic problems, image classification, and LLM pretraining.
watch_item: The favorable convergence guarantees rely on bounded iterates and regularity assumptions, so performance may degrade if these conditions do not hold in practice.
